doc:
The Python client of the OpenHAL hub's local API.

    from openhal.client import connect

    with connect() as hub:
        print(hub.read("plant-waterer", "soil_moisture").value)
        decision = hub.action("plant-waterer", "water", duration={"value": 20, "unit": "s"})
        print(decision.status, decision.message)

The client makes no safety decisions. The hub's kernel decides every command, and a blocked
command comes back as a `Decision`, not an exception. See docs/interfaces/PYTHON.md.

items.name: connect
items.signature: connect(url: str | None = None, token: str | None = None, *, home: Path | str | None = None, timeout: float = 15.0, transport: httpx.BaseTransport | None = None, check: bool = True) -> Client
items.doc:
Open a blocking client to the hub.

With `check` it calls `/v1/whoami` first, so a wrong address or token fails here.

fields.doc: Set when the command waits for a human.

fields.name: ok
fields.doc: False when the driver could not read. `error` says why.

fields.name: bytes
fields.doc: Length of a binary value, which is not returned inline.

fields.name: protocol_version
fields.doc: The hub protocol version, for example 2026-10-24.

fields.name: conformance
fields.doc: The hub's conformance level, core, control or full.

fields.name: allow_lan
fields.doc: True when other machines may connect with a paired token.

fields.name: stopped
fields.doc: True after a stop until a human unlocks. Every command is refused meanwhile.

fields.name: hazard
fields.doc: low, medium or high. High hazard commands always wait for a human.

fields.name: writable
fields.doc: False while the device file has unconfirmed limits.

fields.name: unavailable
fields.doc: Why the device can't take commands, if it can't.

fields.doc: The driver's conformance level.

items.name: OpenHALError
items.doc: Base class for every client error. `status_code` is the HTTP status when there was one.

items.name: HubNotRunning
items.doc: Nothing answered at the hub address.

items.name: Unauthorized
items.doc: The hub did not accept the token, or no token was found.

items.name: NotFound
items.doc: The device, channel, request, routine or session does not exist.

items.name: NotSupported
items.doc: The hub is older than this client and does not have the route at all.

items.name: Refused
items.doc: The hub understood the call and refused it, for example an agent asking to approve.

items.name: BadRequest
items.doc: The hub could not read the request. `detail` holds the validation problems.

items.name: HubError
items.doc: The hub failed while answering. Check the hub log.
